text:
maya (Product Designer): quick heads-up — I sketched a "soft revoke" flow for API keys. Instead of instant hard-disable, we mark the key revoked and start a 30s undo window with a prominent toast. thoughts?

sam (PM): i like the safety net, but legal asked for an option to immediately revoke in orgs that require it. can we surface a ‘force revoke’ toggle for admins?

jordan (Frontend): implementation Q: is the key still usable during the 30s? that’s the main risk. i assumed revoked keys return 403 immediately but we keep a flag for undo. if live requests could still succeed that's bad.

maya (Product Designer): good call — proposal: on revoke we flag key.status = "revoked_pending" and backend rejects requests with 403. undo endpoint will flip back to "active" within TTL. visual: toast: "Key revoked · Undo (30s)" with keyboard focus on Undo.

lee (Eng Manager): agree with immediate 403. also we need audit events: key.revoked.pending and key.revoked.confirmed. retention: if undone we emit key.revoked.undone. curious how this works cross-region on Dedicated.

maya (Product Designer): canary copy for toast: "API key disabled. Undo (30s) — will become permanent after timer." alternative shorter: "Key disabled — Undo". accessibility: toast needs role=alert + aria-atomic so screen readers notify.

jordan (Frontend): nits: make sure Undo is a true button, not a link, tab order needs to be predictable. also pressing Esc while toast visible should not dismiss without explicit action. screen readers should read the exact consequence text.

sam (PM): what about rotate flow? when user rotates we show ephemeral secret reveal with a download CTA. if they rotate during a revoke undo window, UX gets weird. probably block rotate while pending revoke, or queue a confirm modal.

maya (Product Designer): UX option A: block rotate with a disabled Rotate button + tooltip: "Finish revoke undo window to rotate, or force revoke to continue." Option B: allow rotate but show conflict modal: "This key is pending revoke — rotating will create a new key and confirm revocation." preference?

lee (Eng Manager): prefer A for simplicity. fewer edge cases and race conditions in backend.

jordan (Frontend): for the secret reveal: dobble-check copy and announce for SR: "New secret generated. Copy now — this value will not be shown again." include aria-describedby linking to helper text with contrast-checked color.

maya (Product Designer): empty state for credentials page: propose a two-column layout — left: illustration + single sentence, right: quick CTAs (Create key, Bulk rotate, Grant role). alt text: "illustration: person holding a key" — is that too vague?

sam (PM): add tiny hint under Create key: "Use scopes to limit exposure — learn more" linking to docs. also add a small permission badge on keys list (Read-only / Full) so people don't guess.

jordan (Frontend): accessibility nit: badges need 4.5:1 contrast and screenreader labels like "Perms: read-only". keyboard users should be able to filter by permission via keyboard-only controls.

maya (Product Designer): copy proposal for revoke modal (if we go modal for force revoke): 

```
Are you sure you want to revoke this API key?
Revoking will immediately disable the key across all environments.
[Force revoke] [Cancel]
```

with secondary line: "Admins can force revoke even during undo windows."

sam (PM): also add analytics: revoke_initiated, revoke_confirmed, revoke_undone, revoke_forced. tie to workspace id + actor.

access-bot: policy check: workspace org:acme-corp requires immediate revocation. Force revoke will bypass undo and emit compliance.note.

maya (Product Designer): action items: 1) jordan — keyboard + SR behavior for toast and secret reveal; 2) lee — add audit events and API for undo; 3) sam — update PRD with force-revoke admin toggle; 4) me — mock screens + copy variants. will post Figma link shortly.

sam (PM): timeline: can we prototype this week? if so i'll loop legal to confirm constraints.

jordan (Frontend): can do a prototype for the toast & keyboard flow tomorrow.

lee (Eng Manager): backend ETA on undo endpoint: 2 Sprints. will scope smaller if needed.

maya (Product Designer): Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/cred-soft-revoke — comments enabled. please add exact words you prefer on the toast. :sparkles:
